mainTopic: Whether a לסטים מזוין is treated like a גנב (אביי and רב יוסף, and a rejected proof from a renter), then רב on an animal that fell into a garden.
overview: רב יוסף holds that a לסטים מזוין (armed bandit) counts as a גנב (thief). אביי challenges him twice from ברייתות. First, a ברייתא says a שומר שכר does not pay כפל, but under רב יוסף he would pay כפל for a false armed-bandit claim. רב יוסף answers that a שומר שכר pays כפל only in that one case, unlike a שומר חנם. Second, a ברייתא calls its קל וחומר from a שומר שכר to a שואל unbreakable. רב יוסף answers that paying the קרן with no oath is stricter than paying כפל after an oath. The גמרא then tries to prove רב יוסף's view from a ברייתא about a renter. It rejects that proof three ways: through רבי מאיר, through רבה בר אבוה's reversed version, and through רבי זירא's unarmed-bandit case. Finally, the גמרא turns to the משנה about an animal that fell into a garden. רב says the owner pays for the benefit of a cushioned fall. The גמרא rejects linking this to רב's rule 'הָיָה לַהּ שֶׁלֹּא תֹּאכַל', and its new explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ברייתא's refusal to compare a paid guard to an unpaid guard
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rejects learning the שומר שכר from the שומר חנם, because a שומר חנם pays כפל and a שומר שכר does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. You said this about a שומר חנם, who pays double. Can you say the same about a שומר שכר, who does not pay double?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the end of a ברייתא that refuses to apply a rule from the unpaid guard to the paid guard. This is the base text that אביי is about to use against רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא points to a difference between the two guards: a שומר חנם pays תשלומי כפל (double payment) for a false theft claim, and a שומר שכר does not. Because of that difference, you cannot learn one from the other. Read simply, it sounds like a שומר שכר never pays כפל.

keyTerms.meaning: An unpaid guard who watches someone's item for free
A paid guard who is paid to watch the item
Double payment, the fine a thief pays
'If you said...', a phrase that opens a rejection of a comparison

phrases.english: No; if you said so regarding an unpaid guard,
that is because he pays a double payment,
will you say the same about a paid guard,
who does not pay a double payment?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted at the end of the previous section of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שומר שכר cannot be learned from a שומר חנם, because the שומר חנם pays כפל and the שומר שכר does not.

steps.title: אביי: if an armed bandit counts as a thief, a paid guard would sometimes pay double
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that רב יוסף's view would make a שומר שכר pay כפל in one case, which goes against the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think an armed bandit counts as a thief, then a שומר שכר would pay double when he claims an armed bandit took the item.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's view that a לסטים מזוין counts as a גנב. He uses the ברייתא that was just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שומר שכר does not have to pay if an armed bandit really took the item. So if he lies and says 'an armed bandit took it', he is making a false theft claim. If an armed bandit counts as a thief, that false claim should make him pay כפל. That clashes with the ברייתא's statement that a שומר שכר does not pay כפל.

keyTerms.meaning: An armed bandit
'And if it enters your mind...', which opens a challenge to an idea
He makes the claim of...
A thief, who takes in secret

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ לִסְטִים מְזוּיָּין גַּנָּב הוּא,
phrases.english: And if you think that an armed bandit is a thief,

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצָא בְּשׁוֹמֵר שָׂכָר מְשַׁלֵּם תַּשְׁלוּמֵי כֶפֶל –
phrases.english: it turns out that a paid guard does pay a double payment,
when he claims that an armed bandit took it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ לִסְטִים מְזוּיָּין גַּנָּב הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא from step 1 as a weapon against רב יוסף.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's view that a לסטים מזוין is a גנב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His view would create a case where a שומר שכר pays כפל, but the ברייתא says a שומר שכר does not pay כפל.

steps.title: רב יוסף rereads the ברייתא: a paid guard pays double, but only in one case
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that the ברייתא only means a שומר שכר pays כפל in fewer cases than a שומר חנם, not that he never pays.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: this is what the ברייתא means. A שומר חנם pays double for any false theft claim. A שומר שכר pays double only when he claims an armed bandit took it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends himself by explaining the ברייתא differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'does not pay כפל' now mean 'does not pay כפל in every case'. A שומר שכר must pay for ordinary theft anyway, so a false claim of ordinary theft gains him nothing and brings no כפל. Only the armed-bandit claim, which would free him, brings כפל. The difference between the guards still exists, so the ברייתא's refusal to compare them still works.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is what it means', a rereading of a source
In all of his claims
Only, except

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the גמרא can keep a source while narrowing what its words mean, so that רב יוסף's view stays in place.

phrases.english: He said to him: this is what it is saying:
No; if you said so regarding an unpaid guard,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן מְשַׁלֵּם תַּשְׁלוּמֵי כֶפֶל בְּכׇל טַעֲנוֹתָיו,
phrases.english: that is because he pays a double payment for all his claims,
will you say the same about a paid guard,
who does not pay a double payment
except when he claims that an armed bandit took it.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say a שומר שכר never pays כפל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means a שומר שכר pays כפל only for an armed-bandit claim, unlike a שומר חנם, who pays for every claim.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב יוסף, a שומר שכר who falsely claims an armed bandit took the item pays כפל.

steps.title: אביי's new challenge: the קל וחומר about a borrower
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a ברייתא that learns a borrower's liability for theft and loss from a שומר שכר, calling it a קל וחומר with no refutation.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'it breaks or dies'. That covers only breaking and dying. Where do we learn theft and loss? From a קל וחומר: a שומר שכר is exempt for breaking and dying yet liable for theft and loss. So a שואל, who is liable even for breaking and dying, should surely be liable for theft and loss. This קל וחומר has no refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי opens a second challenge against רב יוסף by quoting another ברייתא. This step sets up the challenge; the problem it causes for רב יוסף is spelled out in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא builds a קל וחומר from the שומר שכר to the שואל. It ends by saying the קל וחומר 'has no refutation'. That claim is the key detail, because a refutation might come from a way the שומר שכר is stricter, which is the kind of point raised in step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him from a ברייתא
A borrower
Broken or died, which are accidents
Theft and loss
A logical argument from a weaker case to a stronger case
There is no refutation against it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not stop here thinking the challenge is finished. The ברייתא's words 'no refutation' are what אביי will use against רב יוסף in the next lines.

phrases.english: He challenged him: 'And it breaks or dies',
phrases.notes: שמות 22:13, about someone who borrows an animal.

phrases.english: I have only broken or died;
theft and loss, from where do we know?
You can say a קל וחומר:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה שׁוֹמֵר שָׂכָר, שֶׁפָּטַר בּוֹ שְׁבוּרָה וּמֵתָה,
phrases.english: Just as a paid guard, whom the Torah exempted for broken or died,
is liable for theft and loss;
a borrower, who is liable for broken or died,
is it not logical that he is liable for theft and loss?

phrases.aramaic: וְזֶהוּ קַל וְחוֹמֶר שֶׁאֵין עָלָיו תְּשׁוּבָה.
phrases.english: And this is a קל וחומר that has no refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב יוסף's answer in step 3, אביי brings a new source against him.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's view that a לסטים מזוין is a גנב, and his reading in step 3
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says its קל וחומר has no refutation. The next lines will show why that seems to clash with רב יוסף's view.

steps.title: אביי completes his challenge: the comparison should be breakable
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that if a לסטים מזוין is a גנב, the קל וחומר from a שומר שכר to a borrower can be refuted. A שומר שכר pays כפל when he claims a לסטים מזוין, and a borrower never does.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think an armed bandit counts as a thief, why does the ברייתא call this argument unbreakable? You can break it: a שומר שכר is stricter in one way, because he pays double when he falsely claims an armed bandit took the item.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes the challenge he started in the last step. He shows that רב יוסף's view would give us a way to break the ברייתא's קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learned a borrower's liability from a שומר שכר and said 'אין עליו תשובה,' meaning nothing breaks the comparison. Under רב יוסף, a שומר שכר has a strictness the borrower lacks: he pays כפל in the לסטים מזוין case. That difference is a פירכא, so the ברייתא should not have called the argument unbreakable.

keyTerms.meaning: An armed bandit, someone who robs by open force
There is no answer against it; the argument cannot be broken
To refute, to break a comparison by showing a difference
Double payment, the penalty a thief pays

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that an armed bandit is a thief
phrases.notes: This is רב יוסף's view, which אביי is attacking.

phrases.english: why is there no refutation against it?
phrases.notes: He is quoting the ברייתא from the last step, which said the קל וחומר can't be broken.

phrases.english: It can be refuted:

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְשׁוֹמֵר שָׂכָר – שֶׁכֵּן מְשַׁלֵּם תַּשְׁלוּמֵי כֶפֶל
phrases.english: What about a paid guard? He is different, since he pays double payment
when he makes the claim of an armed bandit!

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Continuation of the קשיא in step 4
steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ לִסְטִים מְזוּיָּין גַּנָּב הוּא, אַמַּאי אֵין עָלָיו תְּשׁוּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge from step 4. Step 4 quoted the ברייתא, and this step shows how רב יוסף's view clashes with it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's view that a לסטים מזוין is treated like a גנב, so a שומר שכר who falsely claims one pays כפל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a שומר שכר pays כפל in the לסטים מזוין case, he is stricter than a borrower in that way. That would be a פירכא against the קל וחומר, but the ברייתא says the קל וחומר cannot be refuted.

steps.title: Paying the principal with no oath is stricter than paying double after an oath
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that this תנא considers paying the קרן without any option of an oath stricter than paying כפל, which only comes after an oath. So the כפל of a שומר שכר does not break the קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: This תנא holds that having to pay the principal with no way out through an oath is more serious than paying double, which only happens after swearing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends his view. He explains why the כפל of a שומר שכר is not a real refutation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A borrower must pay the קרן outright and cannot swear his way out. A שומר שכר pays כפל only if he chooses to swear falsely about the לסטים מזוין. This תנא weighs the borrower's obligation as heavier, so the שומר שכר's כפל does not make him the stricter one, and the קל וחומר still works.

keyTerms.meaning: The principal, the basic value of the item
The double payment
An oath
Is stronger or more serious

phrases.english: He said to him: This תנא holds
that paying the principal without an oath
is stronger than paying double through an oath.
phrases.notes: The borrower pays the principal with no oath. The שומר שכר pays double only after he swears falsely.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from steps 4 and 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-weighing the two strictnesses: the proposed פירכא is not a real one according to this תנא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Paying כפל makes a שומר שכר stricter than a borrower, so the קל וחומר breaks.
steps.terutzMaskana: Paying the קרן with no oath option is heavier than paying כפל after an oath. The borrower is still the stricter one, and the קל וחומר holds even if a לסטים מזוין is a גנב.
steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף survives אביי's challenge by ranking 'principal with no oath' above 'double with an oath.'

steps.title: A ברייתא about a renter as possible support for רב יוסף
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests support for רב יוסף from a ברייתא. A שוכר whose rented cow was stolen chose to pay instead of swearing, and when the thief is found, the thief pays the כפל to the שוכר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this supports him: If someone rents a cow from his friend and it is stolen, and the renter says 'I'll pay and I won't swear,' and later the thief is found, the thief pays the double payment to the renter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that might back up רב יוסף. This step only quotes the source. The next step explains how it would prove his point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא rules that once the שוכר pays the owner instead of swearing, he takes the owner's place and receives the thief's כפל. The 'לימא' wording tells us this is only a suggested proof, and the גמרא will look at it carefully.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say it supports him? This opens a suggested proof.
A renter, someone who pays to use an item
I will pay and I will not swear

phrases.english: Let us say this supports him:
One who rents a cow from his friend, and it was stolen,
and that one said: 'I will pay and I will not swear,'
and afterward the thief is found,
he pays the double payment to the renter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רב יוסף from אביי, the גמרא now looks for a source that supports him.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's view that a לסטים מזוין is treated like a גנב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a שוכר who paid instead of swearing and receives the כפל from the thief.

steps.title: How the proof works: the renter could have exempted himself with an oath
steps.stepSummary: The proof assumes the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, who holds that a שוכר is like a שומר שכר. Since the renter chose not to swear, he must have been able to free himself with an oath if he wanted.
steps.simpleTranslation: They assumed the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, who says a renter is like a paid guard. And since it says 'I'll pay and I won't swear,' we learn that if he wanted, he could have freed himself with an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind the suggested proof. It sets up the facts the proof needs: the renter is a שומר שכר, and he had the option to swear and be exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי יהודה, a שוכר is liable for theft, just like a שומר שכר. Even so, the ברייתא suggests he could have sworn and been exempt, so there must be some claim that frees a liable guard through an oath. The גמרא is building toward connecting this to the לסטים מזוין case, which would help רב יוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: They assumed it to be
One who is paid for guarding, the same as a שומר שכר
By implication, you can infer
Exempts himself

steps.confusionAlert: 'סברוה' means 'they assumed.' It is the reasoning of the people who suggested the proof, not the גמרא's final word. The proof is still being built.

phrases.english: They assumed it follows רבי יהודה,
who said: A renter is like a paid guard;
and since it teaches: 'And he said: I will pay and I will not swear,'
this implies that if he wanted,
he could exempt himself with an oath.
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. The meaning stays the same.

steps.triggerLanguage: סַבְרוּהָ – כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, דְּאָמַר: שׂוֹכֵר כְּנוֹשֵׂא שָׂכָר דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the assumptions behind the suggested proof from the ברייתא in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's view about the לסטים מזוין claim.
steps.raayaSupportSource: An inference from the ברייתא's wording 'הריני משלם ואיני נשבע,' read according to רבי יהודה, that the שוכר could have exempted himself with an oath.

steps.title: The Renter Must Have Claimed an Armed Bandit, So an Armed Bandit Is a Thief
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes the proof. The renter could only have sworn by claiming a לסטים מזוין, yet the bandit pays כפל, so a לסטים מזוין is a גנב.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? It must be where the renter claimed that an armed bandit took the cow. And the ברייתא teaches that when the thief is found, he pays double to the renter. Learn from this: an armed bandit counts as a thief!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pins down the exact case in the ברייתא and draws its conclusion. It says an armed bandit is treated as a thief.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following רבי יהודה, a renter is like a שומר שכר, who must pay for plain theft. So the only way he could have freed himself with an oath is by claiming an armed bandit, which counts as an accident he is not responsible for. Since that bandit still pays כפל, which only a thief pays, the armed bandit must be a גנב, just as רב יוסף holds.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the exact circumstances?
An armed bandit who takes things openly by force
The double payment a thief must pay
Learn from it; conclude from this

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
Is it not where he states
a claim that an armed bandit took it?
And it teaches: and afterward the thief was found,
he pays the double payment to the renter.
Learn from it:
an armed bandit is a thief!

steps.triggerLanguage: היכי דמי כגון דקא טעין טענת לסטים מזויין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the proof begun in steps 7-8 by naming the specific claim and drawing the conclusion.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's view that a לסטים מזוין has the status of a גנב
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the rented cow, read according to רבי יהודה (שוכר is like a שומר שכר)

steps.title: Maybe the ברייתא Follows רבי מאיר, Who Treats a Renter Like an Unpaid Bailee
steps.stepSummary: The proof only works if the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה. If it follows רבי מאיר, the renter could swear on a plain theft claim, and the thief is an ordinary thief.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: Do you assume this follows רבי יהודה, who says a renter is like a paid bailee? Maybe it follows רבי מאיר, who says a renter is like an unpaid bailee.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof by questioning which תנא the ברייתא follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שומר חנם does not pay for theft, so he can free himself with an oath even by claiming an ordinary theft. If the renter is like a שומר חנם, he never needed to claim an armed bandit. The thief who pays כפל could be a plain thief, so nothing is proven about an armed bandit.

keyTerms.meaning: They say; the גמרא's way of opening a response
Perhaps
An unpaid watchman, not liable for theft or loss
A paid watchman, the same as a שומר שכר

phrases.english: They say: do you think
it follows רבי יהודה, who says:
a renter is like a paid bailee?
Perhaps he holds like רבי מאיר,
who says: a renter is like an unpaid bailee.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 9 by attacking its assumption from step 8 that the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof for רב יוסף from the renter ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה; under רבי מאיר the renter can swear on an ordinary theft claim, so the thief need not be an armed bandit.

steps.title: Or Reverse the Opinions, as רבה בר אבוה Teaches
steps.stepSummary: A second rejection: according to רבה בר אבוה, it is רבי יהודה who says a renter is like a שומר חנם. So even following רבי יהודה, there is no proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it follows רבה בר אבוה, who reverses the opinions and teaches: How does a renter pay? רבי מאיר says like a paid bailee; רבי יהודה says like an unpaid bailee.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another way to reject the proof by switching which תנא holds which view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 needed the ברייתא to follow רבי מאיר instead of רבי יהודה. Here the גמרא can even keep the ברייתא as רבי יהודה's view, because in רבה בר אבוה's version רבי יהודה treats a renter as a שומר חנם. Either way, the renter could swear on a plain theft claim, so the proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say; it introduces another possible answer
Reverses; switches the names of who holds which opinion
An אמורא who teaches the dispute about a renter in reversed form

phrases.english: If you want, say
like רבה בר אבוה, who reverses the opinions and teaches:
How does a renter pay?
רבי מאיר says: like a paid bailee;
רבי יהודה says: like an unpaid bailee.

steps.triggerLanguage: איבעית אימא כדמחליף רבה בר אבוה ותני
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second rejection of step 9 that keeps the ברייתא as רבי יהודה's view but reverses the opinions.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof for רב יוסף, even if the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The assumption that רבי יהודה holds a renter is like a שומר שכר; in רבה בר אבוה's version he holds a renter is like a שומר חנם.

steps.title: רבי זירא: He Claimed an Armed Bandit, but It Turned Out to Be an Unarmed One
steps.stepSummary: Even if a renter is like a שומר שכר, the case may be that he claimed an armed bandit, but the robber turned out to be unarmed. An unarmed bandit is a plain thief, so he pays כפל, and nothing is proven about an armed bandit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: What case are we dealing with here? Where the renter claimed an armed bandit took it, and it turned out to be a bandit who was not armed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא gives a third way to reject the proof, without changing anyone's opinion. He reads the case differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The renter really did claim an armed bandit, which is why he could have freed himself with an oath. But the person found was actually an unarmed bandit, who is clearly a thief and pays כפל. So the ברייתא says nothing about whether a real armed bandit counts as a thief.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? It sets up a narrower reading of a source
Claims; makes a claim in court
Who is not armed

steps.whatToRemember: The proof that a לסטים מזוין is a גנב is rejected three ways: maybe the renter is like a שומר חנם (רבי מאיר), maybe the opinions are reversed (רבה בר אבוה), or the bandit turned out to be unarmed (רבי זירא).
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי זירא is saying an armed bandit pays כפל. In his case the robber who pays turned out to be unarmed, so the question about a real armed bandit stays open.

phrases.english: רבי זירא said:
With what are we dealing here?
Where he claims that an armed bandit took it,
and it turns out to be a bandit who is not armed.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי זירא אמר הכא במאי עסקינן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, independent rejection of step 9. It accepts that a renter is like a שומר שכר but redefines the case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The conclusion that a לסטים מזוין is a גנב
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes the bandit who was found was armed; he may have been unarmed even though the renter claimed an armed bandit.

steps.title: רב explains the animal's benefit as a cushioned fall
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: an animal that fell into a garden and benefited pays for its benefit. רב explains that this is a case where the plants softened its fall.
steps.simpleTranslation: If an animal fell into a garden and benefited, its owner pays for the benefit. רב said: this means the plants cushioned the animal when it hit the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה, and רב explains what kind of 'benefit' it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fall itself was an accident, so the owner does not pay for the damage. He still pays for the benefit his animal got. רב says the benefit is that the soft plants saved the animal from getting hurt.

keyTerms.meaning: It (the animal) fell into a garden
Benefits, gets something good out of it
The value of what it benefited
It struck the ground; here, its fall was softened by the plants

phrases.english: If it fell into a garden and benefited,
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה, talking about an animal.

phrases.english: it pays for what it benefited.
Rav said: where it struck the ground and was cushioned.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְלָה לְגִינָּה וְנֶהֱנֵית – מְשַׁלֶּמֶת מַה שֶּׁנֶּהֱנֵית. אָמַר רַב: בְּנֶחְבְּטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, separate from the armed bandit discussion in steps 1–12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The benefit the owner pays for is the cushioning of the fall.

steps.title: Inference from רב and a suggested link to his other ruling
steps.stepSummary: From רב's words the גמרא infers that if the animal ate, the owner pays nothing, not even for the benefit. It asks whether this follows רב's known rule: 'the animal should not have eaten.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that if the animal ate, the owner does not pay even for the benefit. Shall we say רב is following his own reasoning, since רב said: 'it should not have eaten'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from רב's explanation. Then it suggests that this conclusion comes from another ruling of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב limited the payment to the cushioned fall, so eating the plants seems to bring no payment at all. The גמרא suggests a reason: in another case רב said the animal 'should not have eaten,' so the eating is blamed on the animal. Here too, the eating would be blamed on the animal and not on its owner.

keyTerms.meaning: It (the animal) ate
Shall we say? (introduces a suggestion)
Following his own known reasoning
It should not have eaten (רב's known rule)

phrases.english: But if it ate,
it does not pay even for what it benefited.
Shall we say Rav follows his own reasoning,

phrases.aramaic: דַּאֲמַר רַב: הָיָה לַהּ שֶׁלֹּא תֹּאכַל?
phrases.english: as Rav said: it should not have eaten?
phrases.notes: This points back to רב's case: produce was left in someone's yard without permission, and the yard owner's animal ate it and got sick. The produce owner is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from רב's explanation in step 13 and proposes where it comes from.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רב's ruling here come from his rule 'הָיָה לַהּ שֶׁלֹּא תֹּאכַל'?

steps.title: The two cases are not alike
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the link. רב's rule 'it should not have eaten' only lets the produce owner avoid paying when the animal got hurt. It never lets the animal's owner avoid paying when his animal damages someone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: How can you compare? רב said 'it should not have eaten' where the animal itself got hurt. Then the produce owner can say: 'I won't pay, it should not have eaten.' But when the animal damages someone else's things, did רב ever say the owner is exempt from paying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from step 14 by showing that רב's two cases work in opposite directions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב's other case, 'it should not have eaten' is an argument for the produce owner, so that he does not have to pay for the animal's injury. In the garden case, the animal is the one doing the damage. Using the same argument to free its owner from paying would turn רב's rule upside down.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare these? (strong rejection)
It (the animal) was harmed
The owner of the produce
To cause damage

steps.whatToRemember: 'הָיָה לַהּ שֶׁלֹּא תֹּאכַל' is a shield for the produce owner when the animal gets hurt. It is not a shield for the animal's owner when the animal does damage.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two sides. In רב's rule the animal is the victim. In the garden case the animal is the one causing the damage.

phrases.english: They say: How can you compare?!
Say that Rav said there
'it should not have eaten'
where it itself was harmed,
since the owner of the produce can say to him:
'I will not pay; it should not have eaten.'
But where it damages others,
that it is exempt from paying, did he say that?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the link suggested in step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects tying רב's garden ruling to his rule 'הָיָה לַהּ שֶׁלֹּא תֹּאכַל'.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That rule frees the produce owner when the animal is injured. It cannot free the animal's owner when the animal causes damage.

steps.title: Setting up a new explanation
steps.stepSummary: The word אֶלָּא ('rather') opens a new explanation of רב's ruling. The explanation itself continues on the next amud.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. Having rejected the suggested reason, it is about to give a different explanation of רב's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אֶלָּא tells us the earlier idea is dropped and a new one is coming. The actual explanation appears in the next part of the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the previous idea and introduces a new one)

phrases.english: Rather,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the suggestion in step 15, it opens a new explanation of the inference from step 14.
